question: What is the difference between the compound interests on Rs. 25000 for 1 year at 6% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly? (In Rs.)
solution:
**Given:**

Principal(P) = Rs. 25000

Time period(T) = 1 yr

Rate of interest(R) = 6%

**Formula used:**

C.I₁ = P× bigg(1+dfrac{R}{200} bigg)²t- P (for compounded half-yearly)

C.I₂ = P× bigg(1+dfrac{R}{100} bigg)^t- P (for compounded yearly)

**Calculation:**

C.I₁ = 25000× bigg(1+ dfrac{6}{200} bigg)² - 25000 

⇒ 25000× bigg(dfrac{103}{100} bigg)² - 25000 

⇒ 26522.5 - 25000 = Rs. 1522.5

C.I₂ = 25000× bigg(1+ dfrac{6}{100} bigg) - 25000

⇒ 25000 × 106over100 - 25000

⇒ 26500 - 25000 = Rs. 1500 

Difference between compound interests compounded half-yearly and yearly = 1522.5 - 1500 = Rs. 22.5.

**∴ The answer is Rs. 22.5.**
